title: State diagram on ELK: Mermaid's handover order and composite directions, notes kept in their block

v:
## Context

The state diagram moves onto the shared ELK layout core (`layout/directedGraph/`), the third kind after the flowchart (`01M4VA67HYZZ1PZG49XA30454N`) and the class diagram (`01M4VHSY2W1Q9E5QCA51F1TCJM`), under the rules of `01M4VANRC6B2C14NHVC2KRZ9Y8`. On dagre the state adapter grew every composite's frame itself (`compositeFrames`), clipped a transition naming a composite back to that frame, and shifted the drawing to hold frames that grew past the engine's extent.

What Mermaid 12.2.0 does, read in its dist (`node_modules/.pnpm/mermaid@12.2.0/node_modules/mermaid/dist/chunks/mermaid.esm/`) and measured in headless Chrome:

- **Handover order.** `dataFetcher` (`stateDiagram-v2-MYRXERYP.mjs`, line 1127) walks the document statement by statement: each state is added where it is first named (both ends of a transition in turn), a composite's members where its block is written, each transition where it is written. A `note` statement adds, at that point, a note group, the note and the link (`state → note` for `right of`, `note → state` for `left of`, line 1222).
- **Composites.** A composite and each concurrent region is an ELK compound node with a direction of its own: the block's `direction`, or `DEFAULT_NESTED_DOC_DIR`, `TB` (`getDir`, lines 964 and 1083). Measured: `direction LR`, `X --> C`, `state C { A --> B }` draws A above B; `direction LR` above `state Active { A --> B -- C --> D }` draws each region's members in a column, as with no `direction`.
- **Boundary-crossing edge.** `configureCrossHierarchyEdges` (`elk-V4PLJRSU.mjs`, around line 99889), as in the flowchart: `X --> A` into a member of `state C { direction LR ... }` stacks A and B; `X --> C` and `C --> C` keep the row.
- **Pseudo-states.** A start or end is a 14px box. ELK keeps a port 12px off each end of a side (`portsSurrounding`), so a route leaves a 14px disc 3px off its centre; `alignDegenerateNodeToAnchor` (`elk-V4PLJRSU.mjs`, line 100618) moves such a box onto the first route that reaches it. Measured: `[*] --> Idle` draws the disc and Idle on one vertical line (both at x 104).
- **Self-transitions.** `A --> A` and `C --> C` on a composite are ELK self-loops, orthogonal runs off one side of the box or the frame.
- **Notes.** The note group has no parent: the note of a state inside a composite is laid out at the diagram's top level, outside the composite. Its link then has ends with different parents, so it voids every composite around the state, and the note group, by the boundary-crossing rule. Measured: `X --> C`, `state C { direction LR  A --> B  B --> D  note right of A : a note }` draws A, B and D in a column and the note below C, outside it, its link leaving the frame; `note right of C` on a `direction LR` composite holding `A --> B` stacks A above B.
- **Connectors.** Every edge ELK routed, transitions and note links alike, is drawn `rounded` (`applyElkEdgeLayout`, line 100401), with line hops.

## Decision

The state adapter (`layoutStateDiagram`) hands the core every composite and region as a cluster (12px padding, the title's measured size, the block's direction or `TB`), every state in the model's order, transitions in the model's order, and each note as a box beside its state with its link; every connector carries the `rounded` corner radius for the line hops. `compositeFrames`, the composite end clipping and the shift are gone; frames, ends on frames, loops and the extent are the core's. A composite's title is drawn where the core puts it, moved along its band off a route (`01M4VFW4XGRGSMTMQ12HME145W`). The core gained `centreSmallBoxesOnRoutes`, Mermaid's `alignDegenerateNodeToAnchor`.

The model does not keep where a `note` statement was written, so each note is handed over as if written right after the statement that first names its state: its box right after the state, its link right after the first transition naming the state (after every transition when none does). Measured on the state parity fixtures: handing every link over after every transition draws `state-long-labels` mirrored left to right against Mermaid (horizontal agreement 33.3% on it, 89.2% pooled); this rule gives 100% on it and 90.8% pooled.

One departure from Mermaid 12, under rule 1 of `01M4VANRC6B2C14NHVC2KRZ9Y8`:

**A note is laid out at the level of the state it annotates, and its link voids no direction.** Mermaid's picture contradicts the document twice: a note written inside `state C { ... }` about a state in C is drawn outside C, and writing a note makes the block give up the `direction` its author wrote. Siren keeps the note inside the block, and the link's two ends share a parent, so no direction is voided. Measured on the first document above: Siren draws A, B and D in C's `LR` row with the note inside C; Mermaid stacks them and draws the note below C, its link running 290px from A out of the frame. A note on the composite itself sits at the composite's own level beside its frame, and the composite keeps its `direction`.

Measured, no change: transition labels and note links in a composite's title band. Note links are routes and already block a title (`placeTitlesClear`). Over the state parity fixtures, the repo's state examples and 400 random state documents (two titled composites each, labelled transitions, composite self-transitions, notes inside and on composites, every document direction), no transition's centre label overlapped a composite's title; ELK places a centre label in a layer, never in a band. So centre labels are not added to the title's obstacles.

## Evidence

Gate (rule 8 of `01M4VANRC6B2C14NHVC2KRZ9Y8`), parity over the four state fixtures (`example-state-core`, `example-state-reveal`, `state-long-labels`, `state-composites`), Siren against Mermaid 12.2.0 default in headless Chrome:

| Measure | Siren on ELK | Siren on dagre (before) | Mermaid | Gate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Through unrelated boxes | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Crossings | 0 | 1 | 0 | at most 110% of Mermaid's |
| Vertical agreement (pooled, 65 pairs) | 100.0% | 87.7% | | at least 90% |
| Horizontal agreement (pooled) | 90.8% | 66.2% | | at least 90% |
| Failures | 0 | 0 | | 0 |
| Through titles | 1 | 0 | 1 | |
| Reversals | 0 | 1 | 1 | |

Five of the six disagreeing pairs are `example-state-reveal`, a single column: Mermaid draws its four matched states at one x exactly; Siren's sit at one x in its SVG, and the page's client rects, read some 30,000px down the parity page, differ by a few millionths of a pixel. The parity metric normalizes each axis to the matched nodes' extent, so a sub-pixel extent turns into a full one. Without that fixture the pooled horizontal agreement is 58 of 59 pairs.

The gate passes. The 11 flowchart fixtures are unchanged (crossings 176 against 176, vertical 99.6%, horizontal 97.8%, through-nodes 0, through-titles 15), and so are the three class fixtures (0 crossings against 0, 0 through-nodes, 97.3% / 100%).

## Consequences

Every state diagram's picture changes: orthogonal rounded transitions with line hops, frames from the engine, a composite that names no direction laid out top to bottom whatever the document's direction, pseudo-states on the line of their transition. The dagre-era divergence where an undirected composite or region followed a document-level `LR` (backlog `01M36SJDN`) is gone.
